turns.content: In triangle ABC, BC=12 square units and angle B=30 degrees. Let AC=b and AB=c, and identify which side is opposite the given angle.
Apply the Law of Cosines to derive the quadratic equation for c. Use its discriminant to find the range of AC measured in degrees that gives two distinct real values of c.
Use the root sum and product to determine when both possible values of c are positive.
Check whether either boundary value gives two distinct positive lengths.
List the admissible integer values of b.
Count the integer cubic units of AC for which two distinct positive values of AB are possible.
